query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Addition of approximately 3 at.% tungsten (W) to the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix will promote the in-situ formation of a continuous, adherent tungsten oxide (WO3) tribolayer during sliding, thereby yielding consistently lower friction and wear from room temperature up to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogeneous CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy produced via conventional melting methods, exhibiting a single-phase microstructure.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by adding ~3 at.% tungsten during melting, ensuring W is uniformly distributed in the matrix so that under sliding conditions it can oxidize in situ.
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted in ambient air with controlled normal loads (e.g., around 10 N) and representative sliding speeds over the temperature range from approximately 25 °C (room temperature) to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Development of a coherent, adherent WO3 tribofilm on the worn surfaces during sliding.
generation.mechanism: During sliding, tungsten at or near the surface oxidizes to form WO3. This tungsten oxide layer acts as a solid lubricant by lowering shear resistance at the sliding interface. Its stability across a broad temperature range helps maintain low friction and reduces wear, countering the challenges faced by the baseline alloy when the oxide film is not optimized.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the undoped CoCrFeNi alloy, the tungsten-doped variant is expected to exhibit a significantly lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate throughout the full temperature range, from room temperature up to 800 °C, due to the formation of the stable WO3 tribolayer.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, which tends to develop less effective or non-uniform oxide scales and therefore shows elevated friction and wear, particularly at high temperatures.
generation.boundary: This intervention is applicable for sliding tests in ambient air under controlled load and speed conditions. The beneficial effects are expected only under conditions where oxidation occurs (i.e., in oxidizing environments) and may not apply in vacuum or inert atmospheres, nor under drastically different loading regimes.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal tungsten content to ensure continuous and durable WO3 formation, the kinetics of tribolayer development during short-duration tests, and possible interactions with other oxide species remain uncertain and may require further optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of standard CoCrFeNi alloy and another set modified with 3 at.% tungsten. Subject both to identical sliding wear tests in ambient air over the temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C. Characterize worn surfaces by SEM/EDS and XRD to confirm the formation and continuity of the WO3 tribolayer. Simultaneously measure the coefficient of friction and wear rate.
measurements: Coefficient of friction as a function of temperature
Wear rate (e.g., mass loss or wear volume) across the temperature range
Surface characterization (SEM/EDS, XRD) to identify the presence and morphology of WO3
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-doped alloy does not consistently exhibit a significantly lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate compared to the baseline, or if a coherent WO3 tribolayer cannot be confirmed on the worn surfaces, then the hypothesis is rejected.
